schema_note: Fixture allowlist for the synthtwin data-provenance guard (plan D13). Each entry in 'fixtures' binds one committed data fixture to its origin and must contain exactly these keys: 'path' (repository-relative POSIX path of the committed fixture file), 'generator' (repository-relative path of the seeded script that rebuilds the fixture; invoked as: python <generator> --seed <seed> --out <output-path>), 'seed' (integer seed; the same seed must always produce the same bytes on every platform), 'sha256' (64-character lowercase hex digest of the committed fixture bytes), and 'justification' (a written sentence explaining why this fixture must be committed instead of being built at test time). The checker tools/provenance/check_provenance.py re-runs every generator and byte-compares its output to the committed file; any difference fails. Both 'path' and 'generator' must be repository-relative (no absolute paths, no '..' components), must stay inside the repository, and must be tracked by git once the repository has commits. Generators are executed through tools/provenance/guard_runner.py, which installs a Python audit hook before the generator code runs; the hook refuses imports of network, process, and native-capability modules and blocks the known socket, process-creation, and native-call audit events. That runner is a best-effort in-process guard, not a sandbox or a confinement mechanism: repository source review of every generator script and the CI checks are the operative controls (CI is the authoritative automated verification; from Phase 3's visibility flip the branch ruleset makes it a mechanically enforced merge requirement - see SECURITY.md's activation record). JSON is treated as a data format: a tracked .json file is allowed only if it is one of the checker's known configuration files (KNOWN_CONFIG_JSON in the checker) or listed here. Committed fixtures must be tiny (at most 100000 bytes). Three are committed: the numeric reference vectors of Phase 1 and the two files of Phase 2's generation reference vectors, which are one oracle in two files because the cap leaves no room for one. All three are mathematics rather than data - they contain no value taken from any table, and each generator imports none of the code the vectors check.

fixtures.justification: The twin cells synthtwin's generation method requires for the six cases docs/spec/generation-method-v1.md section G14.3 adds beside its first nine, computed from that specification alone. Four exist because review item P2-C3-F3 found that the nine reached no unrepresentable column, no joint class-and-alphabet packing of free text, no fold collision that a case change cannot build, and no cell carrying the literal decimal, leading-zero or leading-plus style; the fifth exists because review item P2-C4-C3 found that none of them carried a seconds field of 60, the one published end the ordinal space cannot hold. A defect or a withdrawn rule on any of those branches left every committed byte unchanged. This file is written by the same oracle as tests/reference/generation-reference-vectors.json, through the second entry point beside it, and shares that oracle's transform and its proof layer; it is a second FILE only because a committed fixture must stay under the 100000-byte cap and the nine cases already spend 88207 of it. Everything the first entry says of itself holds here: the vectors are a pure function of the uint64 words the file carries as inputs, the recorded seed is accepted and ignored, every binary64 published is proved correctly rounded or proved exact by integer comparison against the midpoints to its neighbours, and the run refuses a full-generator mutant before it writes a byte. The registered generator here is the second ENTRY POINT rather than the oracle itself, and its imports are stated literally (review item P2-C4-C4): it imports os, runpy and sys, and nothing else; it holds no transform and no proof layer of its own; and it executes the oracle beside it by one fixed sibling path, which is the file that imports only argparse, datetime, fractions, json, math, struct and sys. Neither file imports synthtwin, numpy or pandas. No value in this file comes from any real or synthetic table.

The twin cells synthtwin's generation method requires, for the nine cases docs/spec/generation-method-v1.md section G14.3 names, computed from that specification alone. They are committed rather than built at test time for the same reason the numeric vectors are: their whole purpose is to be an oracle the implementation cannot influence, and a value recomputed beside the code it checks could drift with it. The vectors are a pure function of the uint64 words the file itself carries as inputs; the generator holds no random generator and no seed handling, so the recorded seed is accepted and ignored. It imports only argparse, datetime, fractions, json, math, struct and sys - never synthtwin, never numpy, never pandas. numpy could not be imported here in any case: this runner's audit hook refuses ctypes and numpy imports ctypes, which is why the transform from words to bytes is written in exact standard-library integer arithmetic. Every binary64 the file publishes is proved correctly rounded, or proved exact, by integer comparison against the midpoints to its neighbours, and the run refuses a full-generator mutant before it writes a byte. No value in this file comes from any real or synthetic table.

Reference values for the profiler's mean, standard deviation, skewness and percentile ladder, computed by exact rational arithmetic. They are committed rather than built at test time because their whole purpose is to be an oracle the implementation cannot influence: a value recomputed beside the code it checks could drift with it, and round 1 of the Phase 1 review found exactly that defect in the golden hash. The generator imports only fractions, decimal, json, math and struct - never synthtwin, never numpy, never pandas - and every float64 it reports is proved correctly rounded by exact integer comparison against the midpoints to its neighbours. No value in this file comes from any real or synthetic table.
